title: Baroque Music and Johann Sebastian Bach
text: Baroque music is a style of Western classical music composed from approximately 1600 to 1750. The baroque period saw the development of functional tonality, opera, and the concerto and sonata forms. Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) is considered the supreme master of Baroque composition, with works including The Well-Tempered Clavier, the Brandenburg Concertos, the St. Matthew Passion, and The Art of Fugue. George Frideric Handel composed Messiah (1741), one of the most frequently performed choral works in Western music. Antonio Vivaldi wrote The Four Seasons. Baroque music is characterized by elaborate ornamentation, polyphonic textures, basso continuo, and dramatic contrasts of dynamics.
